subject: Getting tables to look nice in Word

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Getting tables to look nice in Word
parts:
I'm using the preview version of Rstudio, with the new output to Word document feature - which is pretty nice.

But I'm struggling to make tables come out in Word documents. Is there a way to persuade Knitr to produce a Word table?

Thanks,

Jeremy

.

messages.author: 8502567f9dbc7c7e
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Getting tables to look nice in Word
parts: I think the simple answer is no, because knitr does not produce docx directly. The useful answer would be that you should be asking RStudio because the translator they use after knitr probably can if you generate the right variety of markdown table.

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Getting tables to look nice in Word
parts:
Thanks, I've found half an answer, which is to use

results=asis in the chunk header.

But it seems to work sometimes, and not others. I suspect you're right, and it's something about pandoc.

Here's a reproducible example. The first chunk makes a nice table in word, the second doesn't.

```{r , results='asis'} 
#works
library(knitr)
data(iris)
kable(head(iris))

```

```{r , results='asis'}
#doesn't work
for(loop in c(1:5)){

kable(head(iris))

}

```

Jeremy

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Getting tables to look nice in Word
parts:
Thanks, I've installed that latest version - it helped, but it's still not happy.

As soon as I put anything else in, it seems that it messes with the table format, so:


```{r , results='asis' , echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
for(loop in c(1:5)){
  print(loop)
  kable(head(iris[c("Sepal.Length", "Sepal.Width")]))
  cat("<br>x<br>")
  }
```

Will produce only the last table properly.

The other tables look like:

| Sepal.Length| Sepal.Width| |------------:|-----------:| | 5.1| 3.5| | 4.9| 3.0| | 4.7| 3.2| | 4.6| 3.1| | 5.0| 3.6| | 5.4| 3.9| [1] 2


and because of the [1] 2 (I'm guessing) pandoc can't convert them to a table.


I've tried inserting a manual line break, using \n or <br> but this doesn't seem to work.


Thanks,


Jeremy


P.S. I was at your talk last night - great talk.

Hi Jeremy,

perhaps good to know you can also directly create Word (and PPT) documents and tables from R, see the ReporteRs package. To play around with the package I made a silly toy example how to use it with R/Shiny, see here. The ReporteRs package is pretty well documented and relatively easy to use.

best Herman

messages.author: 9ec69ca07f36d6a1
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Getting tables to look nice in Word
parts:
If you want to be able to create complex tables, having R output LaTeX markup and running a convertor to create HTML allows the most flexibility.  See http://biostat.mc.vanderbilt.edu/SweaveConvert

Another good option is LaTeX -> xml -> html -> Word, using the latexml system.

Frank
